title: Gruesome Playground Injuries by Rajiv Joseph at the Lucille Lortel Th...
transcript: I had high hopes for Gruesome Playground Injuries but it was a little underwhelming. Not to discredit its reliably great actors Kara Young and Nicholas Braun, but things felt a little too sparse. It's a tricky play — just two characters drifting and reconnecting over 30 years with a through line of pain and suffering, physical and otherwise. They're both pretty messed up, for lack of better terms, and they somehow always find the sickest ways to be seen by each other, as if they don't otherwise know how. It's pretty amusing, though not necessarily laugh-out-loud funny, nor is it super cathartic despite its melancholy undercurrent. The dialogue is emotionally clear and darkly humorous, much like the other works I've seen by Rajiv Joseph, but this one is especially reliant on its dialogue as opposed to its plot to keep you engaged. And while the nontraditional structure and fractured timeline is interesting at first, things don't really peak and valley dramatically, which makes it fall a little flat. Still, Kara Young and Nicholas Braun are both serviceable in these roles that require some beefing up. The amount of actual information we’re given about them is pretty scarce, but they color things in as much as they can, under the stark and understated direction. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
